references.text: Also addresses sins committed through negligence (בִשְׁגָגָה) and the requirements for sin offerings.
Describes cases where someone sins without knowing it and later becomes aware of their guilt.
Elaborates on the laws concerning unintentional sins and the necessary sacrifices for atonement.
A prayer for forgiveness for hidden sins (שְׁגִיאוֹת), which correspond to unintentional sin.
Warns against making hasty vows to God, calling it an unintentional sin.
Speaks of the high priest who can have compassion on those who wander in ignorance (τοῖς ἀγνοοῦσιν).
Refers to offerings for the people's sins committed in ignorance (ἀγνοημάτων).
Both verses define the basis for guilt and the need for atonement due to involuntary or faithless actions against the Lord's commands.
